newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures amble to higher, spread shine.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures amble to higher, spread shine.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures cut early losses to amble higher by Wednesday midsession in another spread-dominated trade before May's first tender day on Thursday, traders said.
May/July switch trade was again the main feature as operators continued to get out of the May position before the month-long notice period.
"People are getting out of May into July," said one.
May has been under pressure all week amid concerns over the new grading rules which come into effect with the July.
Traders said players were reluctant to risk taking delivery of May coffee in case they have to re-deliver the material under revised grading terms in July.
By the morning recess, May stood $3 higher at $1,535 a tonne after a low of $1,516 while July managed a $4 gain at $1,605 after dipping below the key $1,600 support level.
May/July switch widened further and this morning it was predominantly traded at $70.
May's uncovered positions continued to dwindle, dropping by a large 1,877 lots to 3,815 lots by Tuesday's close. But July rose 1,900 to 10,718.
Midday volume at the exchange reached 3,138 lots.
Traders said there was no fresh fundamental supply/demand news.
New York arabica futures are expected to attract further speculative and local buying to help extend Tuesday's run-up.
But some traders doubt if the run-up would be sustained on the back of small underlying volume.
Broker GNI said in a commentary that the only reason why news of U.S. roaster Folgers raising retail prices was supportive to the market was that it indicated that roasters were short of spot coffee.
Folgers said on Tuesday that it would raise its coffee prices by 20 cents with immediate effect.
Elsewhere, Merrill Lynch said in its bi-weekly commodity report that a rally on the New York coffee market could last until September. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
